verses.1: At that time, the Pharisees and officials from Jerusalem came to Jesus, saying
verses.2: Why do your disciples violate the rules regarding the transmission of the teachings from the elders? After all, they don’t even wash their hands when eating bread.
verses.3: And the one who answered said to them, “Why do you also violate the commandment of God by doing this?”
verses.4: For the God said, “Kill both the father and the mother.” And he also said that those who are evil towards their parents should be punished with death.
verses.5: But you say: “What can one say to one’s father or mother? What gift could be given from me?”
verses.6: He will not honor his father. And you have confirmed the word of God through your obedience.
verses.7: Fakers, Esaias wisely spoke about you, saying:
verses.8: This people honors me with their words, but their hearts remain far away from me.
verses.9: But if you truly respect me, then teach others the principles of wisdom.
verses.10: And when he called the crowd together, he said to them, “Listen and also recite.”
verses.11: It’s not the person who enters the mouth; it’s rather the thing that is carried out of the mouth.
verses.12: Then the disciples came forward and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard his words?”
verses.13: And the one who answered said, “All plants that my father, the Heavenly Father, did not plant will be condemned.”
verses.14: Leave them alone! They are blind guides for the blind. And if a blind person leads another blind person, both of them will fall into a ditch.
verses.15: And when Peter answered, he said to him, “Understand this parable of ours.”
verses.16: And he said, “Are you also ignorant of Akmen?”
verses.17: Don’t you realize that everything that enters the mouth, into the stomach, or into the private parts is also expelled from there?
verses.18: And what is expelled from the mouth and from the heart, it also affects all people in the same way.
verses.19: For from the heart, evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual sins, thefts, false accusations, and insults are born.
verses.20: These are things that are common to all people. But eating food that isn’t properly cooked is not something that’s common among people.
verses.21: And after leaving that place, Jesus continued his journey to the regions of Tyre and Sidon.
verses.22: And behold, a woman from Canaan’s tribe came down from those hills and said, “Have mercy on me, Lord son of David! My daughter is being possessed by demons.”
verses.23: But he did not answer her words. Then the disciples came to him and asked him, “Please stop her from shouting loudly behind us.”
verses.24: But the one who replied said, “It wouldn’t have happened if it hadn’t been for those sheep that were lost in Israel.”
verses.25: And when she came forward, she bowed to him and said, “Lord, help me.”
verses.26: But the one who answered said, “It’s not right to take the bread of the children and give it to the pigs.”
verses.27: And she said, “Yes, my lord. After all, the chickens eat the food that comes from the bowls of their masters.”
verses.28: Then Jesus replied to her, “Woman, your faith has made you well. Do whatever you want.” And the daughter of that woman was healed from that moment on.
verses.29: And after leaving that place, Jesus came near the sea of Galilee. He then climbed up the mountain that stood there.
verses.30: And many people rushed towards him. They were all ill-prepared: some were blind, some were deaf, some were lame, and many others were in similar conditions. He healed them right there by their feet.
verses.31: So that the people might be amazed, seeing those who speak in a simple way, those who are healthy and strong, those who walk with ease, and those who can see despite being blind. And they praised the God of Israel.
verses.32: But Jesus, after inviting his disciples around, said, “I am about to go away from them for three days. They won’t have anything to eat during that time. I don’t want to let them go hungry, even if they must walk on foot.”
verses.33: And the disciples say to him, “Where do we get such a large amount of bread from the desert, so that it can satisfy such a large crowd?”
verses.34: And Jesus said to them, “How many loaves of bread do you have?” They replied, “Seven, and a little fish.”
verses.35: And you ordered the crowd to fall back to the ground.
verses.36: He took the seven kinds of bread and the fish, thanked them, and gave them to the disciples. The disciples, in turn, gave them to the crowd.
verses.37: And everyone ate, and they were satisfied. The remaining portion of the food was filled with seven spouts.
verses.38: The people who suffered were four hundred men, excluding women and children.
verses.39: And after dismissing the crowd, he boarded the ship and arrived at the shores of Magadan.
